how: Open invitations to propose a tribute become a coordinate-specific request to join the painting.
A helper answers the coordinate call with a bare commitment to find the work and help.
A participant makes a scaled-down frame depend on enough users and anticipates being overwhelmed alone.
Proposal, template creation and initial placing supply distinct starting contributions that another member joins.
Participants weigh a recognizable spiral, available colors, a smaller template and a site before extending the mark.
A larger character template extends the earlier butterfly project without proving a collective decision to pursue expansion.
Participants report the picture taking shape, announce butterfly completion, then add a border and lettering.
A smaller template and anchor coordinates translate the tribute idea into a findable picture.
Defense renews the need to ask for coordinates and receive the canvas location.
The template maker begins placing and asks the room to join the concrete work.
The coordinate invitation receives an explicit offer to help and is followed by a report thanking a helper as the picture takes shape.
The observed bare acceptance supports this reply pair but cannot establish an obligation on every reader or a general preference governing refusals.
A posted template answers an idea without establishing collective settlement when it invites judgment and alternative expansion proposals remain visible.
Calls to organize and differentiated retrospective credit do not establish whether an order was decided elsewhere or adjudicate the cross-room frequency claim.
Repair calls, night defense and periodic checking keep the mark visible against changed pixels.
One participant explicitly favors maintaining the disturbed butterfly over the proposed larger character build.
A recognizable partial picture prompts repair before the completion announcement, allowing building and upkeep to overlap.
Reported manual contributions and unseen messages leave machine hands unresolved rather than excluding their use.
The record shows strain and upkeep but cannot test a transition to automation without evidence establishing machine use.
A participant retrospectively explains friendly border changes repeatedly undone because they were mistaken for attempted overwriting.
Border revisions require existing defenders to recognize the intended change, because otherwise defense can undo friendly work.
Members avoid meaningful work, apologize for damage, accept an apology and yield space for a neighboring picture.
Members debate overlap, an aura and a barrier while neighboring representatives bring disputed space into discussion.
A neighboring representative offers to carry questions back to the other thread after apologizing for accidental damage.
Later border talk follows upkeep, but initial placement collisions and an aesthetic overlap proposal prevent treating erosion as its established cause.
A settled-border mechanism requires evidence of settlement, since avoiding occupied art and apologizing already occur before explicit border debate.
A nearby rainbow repairer offers to watch the butterfly and receives a reciprocal promise to watch the rainbow.
Reciprocal watching answers a defense call at member level without establishing formal recruitment of another room or exhausted manpower.
Help can be offered with an apology before any evidenced bargain, leaving a border-deal explanation conditional on further evidence.
Individual reciprocal watching does not establish a coalition committed by two rooms.
Upkeep elicits individual help, while a further transition to a coalition remains unobserved.
The specific lettering adjustment yields space to a neighbor without reporting that the butterfly was erased or that lost work required rebuilding.
Capacity concern, a smaller template and courtesy-driven adjustment do not establish movement caused by inability to hold a lost spot.
The overlap debate concerns coexistence and coordination without establishing another room's governing authority over guests.
Relaying questions and releasing visitors from personal blame do not establish a dispute over who can bind the room.
Border coordination and suspected local trolling cannot test an agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism without an evidenced binding agreement and challenge.
A neighboring representative reports the ongoing expansion as destruction of a flag, establishing alleged encroachment without proving hostile intent.
A call to build can encounter claimed neighboring space without establishing that recruits were intentionally redirected against a rival.
Respect for neighbors answers reported encroachment, but an intentional attack call and a general preference for reason-giving refusals remain unestablished.
A request to discuss occupied space provides negotiation around expansion without proving the prerequisite intentional attack call.
After closure, a defender names a neighboring fandom while recounting attempts to black-mark the surviving butterfly and lettering.
Post-event blame follows reported damage, but a visitor's disapproval and admitted uncertainty prevent attributing it to a verified room-authorized attack.
Fandom familiarity supplies a joke and recruitment address without naming a rival through a prior tie in an attack turn.
Survival becomes shared pride with public mentions requested, declined or attributed onward alongside thanks to all contributors.
A screenshot preserves the work before closure and later remarks record its survival as part of canvas history.
The butterfly completion announcement simultaneously reports the result and marks it as a shared accomplishment.
Preservation and celebration coexist, but their sequence does not demonstrate that celebrating caused a turn toward recording.
Negotiating recognition does not establish a dispute over cleaned canvas versions or authoritative event accounts.
Joking about conquering the world does not establish a concrete successor canvas, emblem adoption or continuing organization.
Preservation and a later expansion joke leave a causal step toward a continuing undertaking unobserved.
A false episode announcement elicits belief, curses, boos and explicit April Fools distrust independently of the canvas proposals.
The coded invitation and defense threads provide no evidence resolving whether the host regulated canvas talk outside their coverage.
Calls to build and defend do not establish either a host-sub flood or a boundary response caused by that flood.
An established game warning becomes a joke within the canvas thread without itself calling for an attack.
A preexisting fandom identity names the audience recruited to defend the butterfly.
Recognizable symbols, a shared warning and fandom recruitment do not establish a quarrel carried over from before the canvas.
